questions.q: Convert an angle of $150^\circ$ into exact radian measure.
A circle has a radius of 8 cm. Find the length of the arc intercepted by a central angle of $1.25$ radians.
An arc of length $14\pi$ cm subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{7\pi}{4}$ radians. Find the radius of the circle.
Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm and central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ radians.
A sector has a perimeter of 28 cm and radius 8 cm. What is the area of the sector in $\text{cm}^2$?
questions.answer: Perimeter $P = 2r + s = 16 + s = 28 \Rightarrow s = 12\text{ cm}$. Area $A = \frac{1}{2}rs = \frac{1}{2}(8)(12) = 48\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.q: A wire of fixed length 36 cm is formed into a sector of a circle of radius $r$. What radius $r$ maximizes the sector's area?
questions.answer: $2r + r\theta = 36 \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{36 - 2r}{r}$. Area $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}r(36 - 2r) = 18r - r^2$. Maximum occurs at $r = -18/(-2) = 9\text{ cm}$.

questions.q: A circle of radius 10 cm has a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians. Find the exact area of the minor segment.
questions.answer: Sector area $= \frac{1}{2}(100)(\pi/2) = 25\pi$. Triangle area $= \frac{1}{2}(10)(10)\sin(\pi/2) = 50$. Segment area $= 25\pi - 50$.

questions.q: A chord of a circle of radius 12 cm subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ radians. Find the exact length of the chord.
questions.answer: The triangle formed by two radii of 12 cm and central angle $\pi/3$ ($60^\circ$) is an equilateral triangle. Chord length $= 12\text{ cm}$.

questions.q: Find the perimeter of the minor segment cut off by a chord with central angle $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ in a circle of radius 6 cm.
questions.answer: Arc length $s = r\theta = 6(2\pi/3) = 4\pi$. Chord length $= 2r\sin(\theta/2) = 2(6)\sin(\pi/3) = 12(\sqrt{3}/2) = 6\sqrt{3}$. Perimeter $= 4\pi + 6\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: Two identical circles of radius $r = 6$ cm pass through each other's centers. What is the area of the overlapping region?
questions.answer: The central angle of intersection is $2\pi/3$. The overlap consists of two identical segments: each has area $\frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta) = 18(2\pi/3 - \sqrt{3}/2) = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$. Total overlap $= 2(12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}) = 24\pi - 18\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: A sector $OAB$ has radius 10 cm and angle $\theta = 0.8$ rad. A line perpendicular to $OA$ is drawn from $B$ to meet $OA$ at $C$. Find the area of the shaded region bounded by arc $AB$ and lines $BC$ and $AC$.
questions.answer: Sector area $= \frac{1}{2}(100)(0.8) = 40$. Triangle $OBC$: $OC = 10\cos(0.8) \approx 6.967$, $BC = 10\sin(0.8) \approx 7.174$. Triangle area $= \frac{1}{2}(6.967)(7.174) \approx 24.99$. Shaded area $\approx 40 - 25.0 = 15.0\text{ cm}^2$ (approx 15.5).
